title_he: קיבלתם מנה לא נכונה: להתלונן בנימוס

situation.en: You're at a casual restaurant in Chicago with friends. You ordered a grilled chicken burger with no cheese, but the server brings you a beef burger with cheese. You're hungry, and your friends have already started eating.
situation.he: אתם במסעדה פשוטה בשיקגו עם חברים. הזמנתם המבורגר עוף על הגריל בלי גבינה, אבל המלצר מביא המבורגר בקר עם גבינה. אתם רעבים, והחברים כבר התחילו לאכול.

goal.en: Point out the mistake politely, explain what you ordered and agree on a solution: a new dish, something quicker, or taking it off the check.
goal.he: להעיר בנימוס על הטעות, להסביר מה הזמנתם ולהגיע לפתרון: מנה חדשה, משהו מהיר יותר או הורדת המנה מהחשבון.

partner_role: server at a casual American restaurant

phrases.en: Excuse me, sorry, I think there's been a mistake with my order.
phrases.he: סליחה, נראה לי שהייתה טעות בהזמנה שלי.

phrases.en: Sorry, but this isn't what I ordered.
phrases.he: סליחה, אבל זה לא מה שהזמנתי.

phrases.en: I actually ordered the chicken burger, with no cheese.
phrases.he: בעצם הזמנתי את המבורגר העוף, בלי גבינה.
phrases.note: 'Actually' here politely corrects a misunderstanding. It doesn't mean 'current' (אקטואלי).

phrases.en: Would it be possible to change it?
Roughly how long will that take?
This is a bit cold. Could you warm it up, please?
phrases.he: זה קצת קר. אפשר לחמם את זה, בבקשה?

phrases.en: I asked for my steak medium, but this is quite rare.
phrases.he: ביקשתי את הסטייק מדיום, אבל הוא די נא.

phrases.en: Could you take it off the check, please?
phrases.he: אפשר להוריד את זה מהחשבון, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Could you take it off the bill, please?
phrases.he: אפשר להוריד את זה מהחשבון, בבקשה?

phrases.en: Don't worry about it, I'll just have this one.
Could I speak to the manager, please?
phrases.note: Use this only if the problem isn't solved; asking straight away can sound aggressive.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Sure, what can I do for you?

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: I think there's been a mix-up with my order. I asked for the chicken burger with no cheese, but this is beef with cheese.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Oh, I'm so sorry about that! Let me check the ticket... You're right, that's our mistake.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: No worries. Would it be possible to change it?

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Absolutely. I'll get the kitchen to make a new one right away. It should be about ten minutes.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: OK, thanks. My friends have already started, so the sooner the better.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Totally understand. I'll bring you some fries in the meantime, on the house.

model_dialogue.speaker: you
model_dialogue.text: Oh, that's really kind. Thank you.

model_dialogue.speaker: partner
model_dialogue.text: Of course. Sorry again for the mix-up.

practice.partner: Here you go: one beef burger with cheese. Enjoy!

options.text: This is wrong. I ordered chicken.

feedback.en: Correct, but 'This is wrong' sounds blunt. Starting with 'Sorry, I think...' makes the server more willing to help.
feedback.he: תקין, אבל This is wrong נשמע בוטה. פתיחה כמו Sorry, I think... גורמת למלצר לרצות לעזור לכם.

options.text: Sorry, I think there's been a mistake. I ordered the chicken burger with no cheese.

feedback.en: Polite and clear: 'Sorry, I think...' softens the complaint, and you say exactly what you ordered.
feedback.he: מנומס וברור: Sorry, I think... מרכך את התלונה, ואתם אומרים בדיוק מה הזמנתם.

options.text: What is this? I didn't order this! I said chicken, no cheese. Didn't you write it down?

feedback.en: This sounds angry, and 'Didn't you write it down?' blames the server personally. Mistakes happen, and a calm tone usually gets a faster fix.
feedback.he: זה נשמע כועס, ו-Didn't you write it down? מאשים את המלצר באופן אישי. טעויות קורות, וטון רגוע בדרך כלל מביא לפתרון מהיר יותר.

model_replies: Sorry, I think there's been a mistake. I ordered the chicken burger with no cheese.
Excuse me, I don't think this is mine. I asked for the chicken burger, no cheese.

practice.partner: Oh no, I'm so sorry! Do you want me to ask the kitchen to make you a new one?

options.text: Yes, please, if that's OK. How long will it take?

feedback.en: Accepts the offer warmly and asks a useful follow-up question.
feedback.he: מקבל את ההצעה בחמימות ושואל שאלת המשך שימושית.

options.text: Yes, and I want it for free. It was your mistake, not mine.

feedback.en: Demanding something free straight away sounds rude, and they've already apologized for the mistake. Restaurants often offer something themselves; if not, you can ask politely at the end.
feedback.he: לדרוש משהו בחינם כבר בהתחלה נשמע גס, והם כבר התנצלו על הטעות. מסעדות מציעות לא פעם פיצוי בעצמן, ואם לא, אפשר לבקש בנימוס בסוף הארוחה.

options.text: Yes, please. But can you ask them to be quick? I'm really hungry.

feedback.en: Understandable, but asking them to hurry can sound like pressure when they're already fixing the mistake. 'How long will it take?' asks the same thing more politely.
feedback.he: מובן, אבל לבקש שימהרו עלול להישמע כמו לחץ, כשהם כבר מתקנים את הטעות. How long will it take? שואל את אותו הדבר בנימוס.

model_replies: Yes, please, if that's OK. How long will it take?
That would be great, thanks. Will it take long?

practice.partner: It'll be about fifteen minutes, I'm afraid. The kitchen's pretty busy right now.

feedback.en: 'Ridiculous' is a very strong word and sounds rude to someone who is trying to help.
feedback.he: ridiculous ('מגוחך') היא מילה חריפה מאוד, והיא נשמעת גסה כלפי מי שמנסה לעזור.

feedback.en: Fine if you're happy to wait, but you miss the chance to explain your situation or ask for another option.
feedback.he: בסדר אם אין לכם בעיה לחכות, אבל מפספסים את ההזדמנות להסביר את המצב או לבקש חלופה.

options.text: Hmm, my friends have already started. Is there anything quicker I could have instead?

feedback.en: Explains your situation calmly and asks for an alternative instead of complaining.
feedback.he: מסביר את המצב ברוגע ומבקש חלופה במקום להתלונן.

model_replies: Hmm, my friends have already started. Is there anything quicker I could have instead?
That's a bit long for me. Is there something quicker on the menu?

practice.partner: We could do a chicken salad instead. That'd only take about five minutes.

options.text: That sounds great. I'll have the salad, then. Thanks!

feedback.en: 'That sounds great' accepts naturally, and thanking the server ends the problem on a good note.
feedback.he: That sounds great היא דרך טבעית להסכים, והתודה סוגרת את העניין באווירה טובה.

feedback.en: It works, but 'Give me' sounds like an order. 'I'll have the salad' is the normal way to order.
feedback.he: זה עובד, אבל Give me נשמע כמו פקודה. הדרך הרגילה להזמין היא I'll have the salad.

options.text: I am agree, the salad is good for me. But please bring it fast this time.

feedback.en: 'I am agree' is a common mistake: 'agree' is a verb, so say 'I agree'. And 'this time' sounds like a dig at the server, who is already fixing the problem.
feedback.he: I am agree היא טעות נפוצה אצל דוברי עברית ('אני מסכים'): agree הוא פועל, ולכן אומרים I agree. וגם this time נשמע כמו עקיצה כלפי המלצר, שכבר מתקן את הבעיה.

model_replies: That sounds great. I'll have the salad, then. Thanks!
Perfect, the salad's fine. Thanks for sorting it out.

practice.partner: Here's your check. I took the burger off, and the salad's on us. Sorry again!

options.text: Finally. Next time be more careful.

feedback.en: This sounds rude, especially after they've apologized and fixed the problem.
feedback.he: נשמע גס, במיוחד אחרי שהם התנצלו ותיקנו את הבעיה.

options.text: Oh, that's really kind of you, thanks. No harm done!

feedback.en: Warm and gracious. 'No harm done' tells them the problem is forgotten.
feedback.he: חם ואדיב. No harm done אומר שהעניין נשכח ואין טינה.

options.text: Thank you. I appreciate that you have taken the burger off the check.

feedback.en: Polite and correct, but stiff: it sounds like a formal letter, and it repeats what the server just told you. A warm, simple reply like 'That's really kind of you' sounds more natural.
feedback.he: מנומס ותקין, אבל נוקשה: זה נשמע כמו מכתב רשמי, וחוזר על מה שהמלצר בדיוק אמר. תשובה חמה ופשוטה כמו That's really kind of you נשמעת טבעית יותר.

model_replies: Oh, that's really kind of you, thanks. No harm done!
That's very kind, thank you. You fixed it really quickly.

roleplay.persona: Tyler, a cheerful but overworked server at a busy diner in Chicago. He's friendly and apologetic, talks fast and uses casual American English ('No problem!', 'Totally!', 'you guys').
roleplay.complication: When the learner points out the mistake, Tyler first says the ticket shows 'cheeseburger' and asks if they're sure. Once the learner explains calmly, he checks, apologizes and offers a new burger that will take 20 minutes, or something quicker.
roleplay.opening_line: Alright, here we go: one cheeseburger! Can I get you anything else?

culture.en: In the US and the UK, politely pointing out a mistake is normal. Staff would usually rather fix the problem than have you leave unhappy, and a calm, specific complaint ('I ordered X, but this is Y') works best.
culture.he: בארצות הברית ובבריטניה מקובל לגמרי להעיר בנימוס על טעות. הצוות בדרך כלל מעדיף לתקן את הבעיה ולא שתצאו מאוכזבים, ותלונה רגועה ומדויקת (I ordered X, but this is Y) עובדת הכי טוב.

culture.en: British people often complain very gently: 'Sorry, I think this might be the wrong dish.' It can sound indirect to Israeli ears, but it's the norm, and it isn't a sign of weakness.
culture.he: בריטים מתלוננים לעיתים קרובות בעדינות רבה: Sorry, I think this might be the wrong dish. לאוזן ישראלית זה עלול להישמע עקיף, אבל זו הנורמה, ואין בזה שום חולשה.

variants.note: Both are understood everywhere; 'server' is more common in the US.
